records.name: Asharan Culture
records.review_note: Source: Bible Section 2.4. The Asharan people and their way of life. Paternalistic imperialism: conquered peoples are 'lost subjects' not enemies. From Keth (hot/dry continent). Gender-alternating rulers every ~250 years. Equal-rank equal-pay social structure. Advanced bureaucracy and literacy. More technologically advanced than Caldor at conquest. Classification as culture (vs faction/empire): the people and their cultural identity, separate from the empire as a governing structure.
records.body:
ASHARAN EMPIRE IDEOLOGY — Cultural Superiority Complex:
- Genuinely more advanced in technology, infrastructure, law, medicine
- This advancement lends credibility to their ideology
- Subjects do experience material improvement
- Creates moral confusion: Is this liberation or imperialism? Both?

ASHARAN EMPIRE IDEOLOGY — Core Belief System:
- Paternalistic imperialism disguised as liberation
- View of themselves: Enlightened, civilizing force
- View of conquered: Subjects who don't understand they're lost without the empire

KETH CULTURE (Asharan Homeland) — Social Structure:
- Hierarchical with empress at top
- Council of advisors below
- Priests/shamans as decision-makers in ritual matters
- Population supports empire (benefits from trade, stability)

records.name: Caldori Coastal Culture
records.review_note: Source: Bible Section 2.4. Pre-conquest culture of Renmark and surrounding coastal kingdoms. Mediterranean feel — warm, busy, salt-aired port culture. Multiple small kingdoms and city-states before empire. Lower literacy, less centralized government than Keth. Name is descriptive placeholder — Bobby may want a different name for this culture.
records.body:
CALDOR (LOCAL) CULTURES BEFORE CONQUEST

Renmark Culture:
- Coastal, maritime focus
- Mediterranean feel and values
- Scribal tradition (writing and record-keeping important)
- Simple life valued (Sero's preference before conquest)
- Some form of local governance (twelve leaders executed by Asharan)
- Poorer, less developed than Asharan Empire but established

Other Caldor Kingdoms:

- Some better, more stable
- Cultural diversity across the continent

records.review_note: Source: Bible Section 2.4. Culture of the walled independent kingdom. Values: isolation as strength, peace through non-engagement, 2,000 years of uninterrupted development. Advanced beyond all other Maren civilizations through that uninterrupted peace. Ruled by one family. Closed to outsiders. Faces inward. Note: CAELDRATH location record already in DB — this is the culture record for its people and way of life.

records.name: Asharan Empire Ideology
records.review_note: Source: Bible Section 2.4. Classification as lore: worldbuilding fact about the universe, not a character or event. UNK because derived from story-bible document, not from canonical files.
records.body:
ASHARAN EMPIRE IDEOLOGY

Core Belief System:
- Paternalistic imperialism disguised as liberation
- View of themselves: Enlightened, civilizing force
- View of conquered: Subjects who don't understand they're lost without the empire
- Central claim: They're freeing people, not subjugating them

Cultural Superiority Complex:
- Genuinely more advanced in technology, infrastructure, law, medicine
- This advancement lends credibility to their ideology
- Subjects do experience material improvement
- Creates moral confusion: Is this liberation or imperialism? Both?

- Empress is supreme ruler but advised by council
- Council includes priests/shamans
- Long-term rule (250 years per empress) allows for consistent policy
- Succession by selection (not blood)—can corrupt or improve based on council choices

The Immortality Ritual:
- Religious/magical ceremony involving blood-wine
- Performed by priests under empress's command
- Kept secret from recipients
- Seen as a burden, not a gift (by priests)
- Grant of immortality is a form of control and assignment

records.body:
# Tab 1

Month/Year

I awoke this morning to the sound of the tavern mistress chasing young ladies out of my bed. Indeed, what a life I lead. As I began to look for my clothes, my head felt very heavy, and I was having an awful time trying to keep it upright. My head and shoulders seemed to sway off the bed, while my body seemed to sway the other direction. I quickly found myself on the floor, face-first, but I had found my pants. After giving up on movement, I collected my thoughts. Then it struck me. Last evening, after another rousing performance…. Oh shit….

A quick rummage through my pants pockets, and oh thank the sweet heavens, the coin purse is still here. There certainly seems to be some well-to-do people in this part of the world. Good to make note of that. Now if I could only remember the name.

As the events of the evening were slowly finding their way to the forefront of my memory, one of the first things to resurface was that of my chance encounter. As I can recall, directly after my performance, I was passing the hat around and accepting my well wishes from the crowd. I asked the keeper for an ale, when I was quickly informed there was a specific man looking to meet with me. I sharply informed the barkeep that I was not interested in those types of meetings. The bartender pulled in close, "He didn't seem the asking type; there is always the back door?"

He glanced over my shoulder and nodded towards where a strange-looking fellow was sitting quietly, all alone in a corner. He was obviously an Asharan, but that is not why he appeared strange. He looked distinctively weathered and without a hint of doubt in himself or a single worry on his mind. However, his clothes had noticeable wear and looked as if he had inherited them from a much older man.

He generously praised my performance and flair for the dramatic. He also tipped generously and offered to buy me a round. Then, as we discussed recent travels, where I had been coming from, what news I had of the world, his demeanor seemed to suddenly change. He was certainly not listening to the news I was so politely and succinctly providing.

He began scanning the room with quiet, deliberate eyes. Not nervously, but as if he was checking who was near and if we could be heard or not. He obviously had a topic on his mind, and he wasn't interested in divulging it to any watching patrons. He asked me to join him in the private room just off the main hall.

"Let's continue this conversation in the sitting; I have it reserved for the entire evening."

Both he and I went to stand. I informed him I was flattered but preferred to take my leave. I thanked him for the generous donation and the drink and went to make my exit.

At this point, he grabbed my arm and said, "I am sorry to do this. But please come with me. I'm an official advisor to the empress. I would like to continue our conversation." Without a sound, a few of their stone-faced warriors had appeared throughout the tavern. Now I was the one surveying the exits. He showed me to a hallway just behind the table he sat at.

He was not sorry and yet continued cordially. Then I understood his silent confidence. This was a man of power and control. I was not going to be able to leave this conversation without his approval.

He led me to a small private parlor just off the main hall. A fire had already been lit. Two chairs faced it. He settled into one as though he had sat in it a thousand times before and gestured to the other.

"What is your name?" He asked almost suspiciously, as if he had already known the answer.

"I am Aldric Chaudry. And you are?"

"I have a job for you."

"I apologize, good sir, I already have a job, one you've just tipped me very well for."

"Deservedly so, and yet, I do not care. How much coin do you make in a month's worth of performances?"

"Well now, don't you know that's rude to ask on a first date?"

"Even after all this time, I still do not understand your culture's nuances. In Ashar, every man's station determines his wage. Everyone of the same rank earns the same. There is no mystery in this. Regardless, I'm willing to pay you a monthly stipend for you to find a person for me."

"Ok, sweetheart, you have my attention. Tell me more about this monthly stipend?"

He obviously did not like the sweetheart. He provided me with a dramatic huff and stern look and replied, "You will get 100 silver every month for the next 1 year. You will be looking for a man who has been traveling for many years. He has lived many lives and knows more about life and the world than any other human ever to exist. He tends to be cranky and solitary; he will not like that I am giving you this job. Which is why you will not say anything about this meeting to anyone. Ever"

And of course, my lips have never breathed a word of that meeting to another living soul.

records.title: The Traveler — Chapter 1 (Origins Draft)

records.body:
"The sea", his father said, not even bothering to look up from his nets. "The sea, the sea. Always the sea." He continued grumbling as he spooled his nets. Eron did not care if no one heard him. He did not want to have this conversation again.

Sero had learned this would not change his father's mind, but that would not stop him from carrying on anyway.

"I will not listen to these oafs argue over copper pieces all day."

"Son, you will do this. It has already been decided. These decisions are not made lightly. It is what is best for the future of our family."

Eron walked to Sero. Carrying his nets, bundled in his arms. He stood next to Sero, facing the opposite direction, and put his free hand on his son's shoulder. As Eron began to perhaps offer some comforting words, Sero sharply pushed his father's hand off his shoulder, turned from the docks, and walked away.

In that moment, Sero wanted nothing more than to carry on walking for centuries to come, never having to work in that musty shop with miserable Menas. As Sero proceeded from the docks, he trudged up the same hill he had been climbing his entire life. The town had grown from this particular road that led from the docks straight through town. It's rumored that when this continent was first discovered by settlers, they landed here first. Making Renmark one of the oldest cities known to humankind. Now as time has gone on, that one road is merely the center of a rapidly expanding territory that soon may need to be called a city.

Well they would need walls for that right? Wait, what makes a city a city and a town, a town?

Nevertheless, Sero proceeded down this main thoroughfare
